purpose: Certolizumab pegol is used to reduce inflammation and treat conditions like rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, Crohn's disease, and moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. It helps relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness, and can slow down damage to your joints. It is also used during pregnancy when other options are not suitable, as it does not cross the placenta much.
how_it_works: Your body makes a protein called TNF-alpha, which can cause too much inflammation when your immune system overreacts. Certolizumab pegol attaches to that protein and blocks it, turning down the inflammation like lowering a thermostat. The 'pegol' part helps the medication stay in your body longer so it works more effectively.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like colds or sinus infections, headache, rash, nausea, urinary tract infections, and injection site reactions such as redness, pain, or swelling where you give the shot.
warnings: Because this medication lowers your immune system, you are more likely to get serious infections, including tuberculosis (TB) — your doctor will test you for TB before you start. Rarely, it can increase the risk of certain cancers, including lymphoma. Do not take it if you have an active infection. Tell your doctor right away if you develop fever, chills, or signs of infection. Avoid live vaccines while on this medication.
typical_dosing: It is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous). For most conditions, the starting dose is 400 mg (given as two 200 mg injections) at weeks 0, 2, and 4, then a maintenance dose of 200 mg every 2 weeks or 400 mg every 4 weeks. Your doctor will decide the best schedule for your condition.
